dossier.public_summary: The dip depth changes dramatically between sectors and the star shows a very strong brightness wobble tied to the same short period, plus a transit duration that does not match the M-dwarf size. With the centroid on the target, this is best explained as a stellar binary/variability system rather than a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor of ~9x between sectors (19360 ppm vs 2056 ppm). With sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source this is not a calibration offset between pipelines, so the signal is not steady as a planet must be.

Large out-of-transit modulation almost as large as the transit depth and highly significant, indicating a phase curve from a close companion/stellar variability rather than a quiet star with a planet.

Transit duration and shape implied density is massively inconsistent with the TIC star density (M-dwarf 0.3208 Rsun), even for an ultra-short 0.785 d period, which positively favours a blended eclipsing binary rather than a planet on the target.

Difference imaging puts the dip on the target and far from any neighbour that could cause it, so a background blended NEB is ruled out and the variability must be intrinsic to the target system (EB-like variability, not a planet).
